I attached the remittance file (see CSV) and the payment trace from our bank. Can you confirm whether Redwood received a multi-currency instruction or if this was aggregated at settlement? We need to close our month‑end here and will need the posting details (journal, clearing) to match our ledger.

On Tue, Apr 11, 2028 at 09:10 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Marco's note — tagging finance leads to investigate.

Thanks Jordan — dug into the payment trace and the AR lines. Summary:
- Invoice INV-44321 (EUR 75,000) shows bank settlement with two legs: EUR 52,500 (70%) and GBP equivalent of EUR 22,500 (converted at bank FX). The GBP leg was posted to AR as a separate subledger transaction under AR-GBP-34 which picked up a different VAT code (UK_VAT_REVERSE) by our tax filter.
- The correct treatment for this customer is EU B2B reverse charge on the entire invoice (no UK VAT), so the GBP leg posting was incorrect.

Proposed remediation entries (high-level):
1) Reverse incorrect VAT posting:
   Dr: VAT_PAYABLE_UK  0 (reverse tax code allocation)
   Cr: AR-GBP-34 (remove tax allocation)
2) Reclass GBP leg to AR-EUR aggregation:
   Dr: AR-EUR-AGG 22,500
   Cr: AR-GBP-34 22,500
3) FX P&L true-up (bank commission/FX realized) — posted to FX_GAIN_LOSS  - see attached template for amounts.

I attached journal_entries_PROPOSED.xlsx with line-level GLs and the suggested journal description. Grace — once you confirm the exact subledger ids and clearing references, we can post a corrective journal. Marcus, this doesn't change revenue recognition timing but will change the currency/ledger mapping we use for reporting — confirm if any deferred revenue staging needs a note.

I'll mark the entries as provisional until we have the AR subledger confirmations and Marco's AP confirms matching amounts.

—Lauren
